title: Free arrows in fixed-object simplicial categories and their evaluation adjunction
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Let $O$ be a small set and $a,b\in O$, allowing $a=b$. For a small simplicial set $K$, define $F^O_{a,b}(K)$ to have object set $O$ and, in simplicial degree $n$, the free ordinary category on the directed graph having one generating arrow $a\to b$ for each element of $K_n$ and no other generating arrows. Its arrows are finite composable words, including the length-zero identity at each object; composition concatenates words. Faces and degeneracies apply to each letter. This construction defines a functor $F^O_{a,b}:\mathrm{sSet}\to\mathrm{sCat}_O$. For every $T\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$, restriction to the length-one words gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}_O}(F^O_{a,b}(K),T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,T(a,b)),$$
natural in $K$ and $T$. The inverse sends a word to the composite of the images of its letters and an empty word to the corresponding identity. Thus $F^O_{a,b}$ is left adjoint to mapping-set evaluation, including when the generators are loops.

source.place: Bergner, Rigidification of algebras over multi-sorted theories, Example 3.5, printed pp.1937-1938, and the evaluation/free adjunction before Theorem 4.7, printed p.1942. Explicit degreewise word construction; no Stacks tag states this enriched adjunction.

proof.text: Fix $O,a,b,K$ as in the statement. In degree $n$, define a word from $x$ to $y$ to be a finite list of edges of the specified graph whose successive endpoints agree, starting at $x$ and ending at $y$; the empty list is admitted exactly when $x=y$. All these are small sets, since finite lists of elements of the small set $K_n$, with endpoint conditions, form a small set. Concatenation is associative because both parenthesizations give the same ordered list; concatenating the empty list leaves a list unchanged. Thus the prescribed degree-$n$ arrows and objects form an ordinary category. No generator is identified with an identity, even when $a=b$.

proof.text: For a simplicial operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, replace every letter $k$ of a degree-$n$ word by $K(\theta)(k)$, retaining all its endpoints and retaining each empty word. This defines a map on each mapping set and preserves concatenation and empty words. For two operators, applying the two letter substitutions equals applying their composite by the functor law of $K$; the identity operator fixes every letter. Hence each mapping set is a simplicial set, concatenation is a simplicial composition map, and the constant empty words are the simplicial identities. The associative and unit equations just checked hold in every degree, so these data are precisely a simplicial category in the sense of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting].

proof.text: For a simplicial map $u:K\to L$, define $F^O_{a,b}(u)$ to fix $O$ and substitute $u_n(k)$ for each letter $k$ of each word in degree $n$. Substitution preserves concatenation and empty words, and commutes with every simplicial operator because $u$ does so on each letter. Identity substitutions and successive substitutions give respectively the identity functor and substitution by the composite. This defines the asserted functor $F^O_{a,b}$. Define evaluation $E(T)=T(a,b)$ and $E(v)=v_{a,b}$; the identity and composition laws for enriched functors make $E$ a functor. Both functors land in the claimed categories from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting].

proof.text: For $T\in\mathrm{sCat}_O$, a fixed-object enriched functor $G:F^O_{a,b}(K)\to T$ restricts on length-one words to maps $r(G)_n:K_n\to T(a,b)_n$, $k\mapsto G_n([k])$. Letterwise simplicial operators take $[k]$ to $[K(\theta)k]$, so the simplicial-map condition on $G$ gives $T(a,b)(\theta)r(G)_n(k)=r(G)_m(K(\theta)k)$. Thus $r(G)$ is a simplicial map. This uses only the meaning of enriched functor and of the mapping simplicial sets in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting].

proof.text: Conversely, for a simplicial map $f:K\to T(a,b)$, fix objects and send an empty word at $x$ to $\mathrm{id}_x$ in degree $n$, and a nonempty word to the successive composite in $T_n$ of its letters' images $f_n(k)$. This is a recursive definition on word length. Induction on the length of a second word shows that evaluation of a concatenation is the composite of the two evaluations: the empty case is the unit law, and adjoining the last letter uses the associative law in $T_n$. Consequently the extension preserves identities and composition. It is simplicial: induction on length gives $T(x,y)(\theta)(\overline f_n(w))=\overline f_m(\theta w)$, since the empty case uses the simplicial identity map, and the next letter uses simplicial composition in $T$ and $T(a,b)(\theta)f_n(k)=f_m(K(\theta)k)$. Thus $\overline f$ is an enriched functor, using the associative, unital simplicial composition specified in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting].

proof.text: Restriction of $\overline f$ to $[k]$ is $f_n(k)$ by the unit law, hence $r(\overline f)=f$. In the other direction, any enriched functor $G$ sends the empty word to its identity; if its value is known on a word $w$, its value on $w$ followed by a letter is $G(w)$ composed with $G([k])$. Induction on length therefore gives $G(w)=\overline{r(G)}(w)$ for all words in every degree. Object maps are both the identity on $O$. These are inverse maps on the stated Hom sets. The argument uses only functor preservation of identities and composition from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting].

proof.text: For $u:K'\to K$, restriction satisfies $r(G\circ F^O_{a,b}(u))=r(G)\circ u$, since both send $k$ to $G([u(k)])$. For a fixed-object enriched functor $v:T\to T'$, restriction satisfies $r(v\circ G)=v_{a,b}\circ r(G)$, since both send $k$ to $v(G([k]))$. Thus the bijection is natural in both variables, which is the Hom-set definition of $F^O_{a,b}\dashv E$. Explicitly its unit is $k\mapsto[k]$, and its counit evaluates words of arrows of $T(a,b)$ in $T$. The first triangle replaces each letter by its one-letter word and then evaluates, recovering the original word; the other evaluates a one-letter word, recovering the original arrow. When $a=b$, all finite words are composable loops, and the same calculations cover every length, including zero. For $a\ne b$ there are no composable lists of length greater than one; neither inverse calculation assumes this distinction. These checks use only the enriched functor laws from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting].

lean.statement: theorem fixed_object_free_arrow_adjunction {O : Type u} (a b : O) : ∃ adj : freeArrowFunctor a b ⊣ mappingSetEvaluation a b, (∀ (K : SSet.{u}) (T : Fixed O) (G : freeArrow a b K ⟶ T), adj.homEquiv K T G = freeArrowGenerator a b K ≫ G.map a b) ∧ (∀ (K : SSet.{u}) (T : Fixed O) (f : K ⟶ T.Hom a b) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (x y : O) (w : ArrowWord a b (K.obj n) x y), (((adj.homEquiv K T).symm f).map x y).app n w = freeArrowWordImage T f n y w)
